seats.title: Secretary of the Treasury
seats.name: Margaret Hale
seats.view: Every dollar we borrow costs us interest for decades. Growth comes from private investment, not federal checks.

seats.title: Secretary of Commerce
seats.name: Daniel Okafor
seats.view: Factories, ports and fiber decide where the next jobs land. We have to build.

seats.title: Secretary of Energy
seats.name: Ingrid Lindqvist
seats.view: Demand on the grid is climbing. Reliable power and hardened communities come first.

seats.title: Secretary of Health and Human Services
seats.name: Luis Reyes
seats.view: A family one illness or one rent hike from ruin is not free to work or move.

seats.title: Secretary of Education and Labor
seats.name: Grace Park
seats.view: Skills are the bottleneck. Degrees and apprenticeships both open doors.

events.title: Hurricane landfall
events.text: A major hurricane has hit {state}. Its counties have had {disasters} FEMA major-disaster declarations since 2000 (OpenFEMA).

options.label: Rebuild as it was
options.note: Fast and familiar. The same places stay exposed.

options.label: Rebuild to stronger codes
options.note: Slower and pricier now, cheaper next time.

options.label: Fund buyouts in the worst flood zones
options.note: Moves people out of harm's way. Some will not want to go.

events.title: The storm returns
events.text: Another storm has struck {state}, hitting the same neighborhoods that were rebuilt as they were.

options.label: Rebuild again
options.note: Voters are asking why this keeps happening.

options.label: This time, rebuild stronger
options.note: A costly lesson, learned.

events.title: Rent squeeze
events.text: Rents in {state} are climbing again. {rent_burden} of households there already spend half their income on rent (ACS).

options.label: Grants to towns that loosen zoning
options.note: More homes over time. Local officials push back.

options.label: Emergency rental aid
options.note: Fast relief. Does not add a single home.

options.label: Leave it to the market and the states
options.note: No federal cost. The pressure keeps building.

events.title: Plant closing
events.text: A major factory in {state} will close next year. Manufacturing employs {manufacturing} of its workers (ACS).

options.label: Retrain workers through apprenticeships
options.note: Takes a year or two to pay off.

options.label: Offer the company incentives to stay
options.note: Saves the jobs for now. Other companies will ask too.

options.label: Let the plant close
options.note: No federal cost. A hard year for the town.

events.title: Chip fab needs workers
events.text: A semiconductor plant under construction in {state} warns it cannot find enough technicians to open on time.

options.label: Fund technician apprenticeships
options.note: Local workers fill local jobs, in about two years.

options.label: Add tax credits to speed the build
options.note: The plant opens sooner. Workers may come from elsewhere.

options.label: Let the company solve it
options.note: No federal cost. The opening slips.

events.title: Rural hospital closing
events.text: A rural hospital in {state} says it will close its doors. {uninsured} of the state's residents have no health insurance (ACS).

options.label: Emergency grant to keep it open
options.note: Buys time. The money problem remains.

options.label: Fund telehealth and broadband instead
options.note: Care at a distance. No emergency room nearby.

options.label: Let it close
options.note: No federal cost. The nearest ER is now an hour away.

events.title: Grid emergency
events.text: A heat wave pushes the power grid in {state} to the edge. Its population grew {growth} from 2020 to 2025 (Census).

options.label: Fast-track new gas plants
options.note: Quick and firm power. Locks in fuel costs for decades.

options.label: Fund transmission and batteries
options.note: Cleaner and flexible. Lines take years to permit.

options.label: Ask residents to cut demand
options.note: No federal cost. Rolling blackouts are possible.

events.title: Western drought
events.text: Reservoirs serving {state} have fallen sharply, and farms and fast-growing cities are competing for the water.

options.label: Pay farms to use less water
options.note: Saves water fast. Some farm towns lose work.

options.label: Fund water recycling plants
options.note: New supply in a few years.

options.label: Leave it to the states
options.note: No federal cost. The states may not agree.
